PSA Grading Drop-Off in Mississauga

By Nathan Wiebe, CPA — collector, and a buyer and seller of cards. Published July 28, 2026.

This page is about one specific place: PSA's own Canadian receiving centre in Mississauga, Ontario, where collectors can drop cards off in person instead of shipping them. If you're still deciding how to submit at all — direct to PSA, through a local shop, or as part of a group submission — our PSA submission guide covers all three routes. This one is just about what the Mississauga location is, where it is, and how in-person drop-off there actually works.

Why PSA Opened a Canadian Office

For years, grading from Canada meant shipping cards across the border to PSA's operations in the U.S. and back — two international crossings, customs paperwork, cross-border shipping costs, and exposure to duties and tariffs along the way. PSA opened the Mississauga facility to take that friction out of the process for Canadian collectors: submissions routed through PSA Canada move under a bundled customs arrangement instead of being taxed individually, so collectors avoid the extra tariffs and international shipping costs that direct cross-border submissions carry. It's a genuinely different experience than mailing cards to California, not just a marketing location.

The Address

PSA Canada's receiving centre is at 5560 Explorer Dr #101, Mississauga, ON L4W 5M3, according to PSA's own site and matching our directory listing for the location. It sits near Toronto Pearson Airport, which is deliberate — PSA has noted the location makes it easy for collectors flying in from elsewhere in the country to drop off or pick up in person. Get directions from Google Maps, or see the full listing in our directory.

Hours

As posted on psacard.com, the Mississauga receiving centre is open Monday to Thursday, 10am to 6pm, and Friday, 10am to 7pm. Hours around statutory holidays can shift, so if you're planning a special trip, it's worth checking PSA's Mississauga info page directly before you go — we'd rather send you to the source than risk printing a schedule that's since changed.

How In-Person Drop-Off Actually Works

Dropping cards off at PSA Canada isn't a walk-in-with-a-shoebox process — PSA has you do the paperwork online first, then bring the cards to match it. Based on PSA's own submission instructions, the flow looks like this:

  • Build your submission through PSA's online Submission Centre before you go, the same as any other route.
  • Organize your cards in the same order they appear on your submission confirmation — it makes checking your items in at the counter faster.
  • Bring your cards along with either the QR code from your digital confirmation or a printed copy of it.
  • Your submission becomes official once PSA physically receives the cards at the counter, not when you complete the online form.
  • After that, you track your submission's progress the same way as any other route — through PSA's own account tools.

In other words: the online submission is the actual paperwork, and the Mississauga visit is where you hand over the cards that match it — not a substitute for the online step.

How to Pack What You're Bringing

PSA's own guidance is that standard cards should travel in a flexible, protective holder — a Card Saver I is the one PSA names specifically — ideally with a soft penny sleeve inside it for extra protection, rather than loose or in a hard case. Top loaders and hard acrylic holders on standard cards can cause delays at intake and won't be returned to you, so leave those at home for anything but genuinely thick items. Double-check PSA's current submission instructions before you pack, since exact packaging requirements are the kind of detail that's worth confirming fresh rather than relying on a guide that could be a season out of date.

What We Couldn't Verify

We're not printing a phone number for this location because PSA doesn't publish one on psacard.com — if you need to reach someone before you go, PSA's online support is the route PSA points collectors to. Turnaround times and current pricing move often enough that we're not quoting numbers here either — PSA's official pricing page has whatever's current the day you check.

Other Ways to Submit From Canada

Mississauga drop-off is one route, not the only one. Plenty of Canadian collectors still ship directly to PSA, and a number of local shops handle submissions on a collector's behalf. Our PSA submission guide walks through all three, including which one tends to fit which kind of collector.
